text:
nina: FYI AcmeCare returned our DPA with three blockers: (1) a tiny dataflow for embeddings, (2) explicit statement on whether embeddings can be reversed to PII, (3) KMS provenance for BYOK. They want answers today.

security-bot: New ticket CS-9121 created and assigned to customer-success (nina). SLA 48h.

sam: quick check 12: they're on hosted right now? BYOK availability differs.

nina: yes hosted today, may request Dedicated later.

eli: short eng answer: embeddings are stored as encrypted numeric vectors in our blob store (default TTL 90 days, configurable). We do not persist raw PII as a separate reversible object. Current analyses show practical reconstruction from modern embeddings is not feasible.

ops: ops can export KMS audit/provenance logs tied to the service account within 48h for hosted keys. BYOK support is only for Dedicated/Private.

sam: drafting a one-paragraph reply for customer-facing copy, will paste below.

eli: include retention and deletion SLOs: deletion events show in audit logs within 24h.

nina: paste draft: "Hi 1212 thanks for the questions. Short answers: embeddings are stored as encrypted numeric vectors (default TTL 90 days, configurable) and we do not store raw PII as a reversible artifact. Research indicates embeddings are not practically reversible to original text. For hosted deployments, encryption keys are managed by Redwood KMS; BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private only. We can provide KMS provenance/audit logs on request and can sign a narrow DPA addendum for embeddings retention. We recommend pseudonymizing direct identifiers before sending if you require minimization. Attached is a minimal dataflow snapshot and a link to our SOC2 data-handling page. Happy to jump on a call if helpful. — Nina, Customer Success"

nina: minimal ASCII dataflow to attach:
user -> redwood-api -> tokenizer -> model -> embedding-store (encrypted, TTL=90d)
backup -> encrypted-blob (KMS)

sam: looks good. sending now and marking onboarding status: evidence requested on tracker.

eli: thanks, will queue ops for the KMS export request.
